site.title: UFO Archives
site.description: Practical guides on UFO Archives, organized for fast browsing and comparison.

pages.title: UFO Report Databases
pages.summary: UFO report databases and catalogues are not a single, unified body of evidence. They are a patchwork of witness-report repositories, government case files, investigative records, bibliographies and archival finding aids, each built for a different purpose.

pages.title: British Files
pages.summary: British UFO records are scattered across departmental series, making search terms, dates, and government provenance essential to finding useful files.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on British Files.

pages.title: Mo D File Purpose
pages.summary: Ministry of Defence UFO records can document public correspondence, policy handling or intelligence assessment rather than one unified investigation.

pages.title: Overseas Reports
pages.summary: Overseas UFO files often reveal how embassies relayed local claims and managed enquiries rather than how officials investigated the events.

pages.title: RAF Searches
pages.summary: Early RAF sightings are easier to locate when searches combine period language with airfields, commands, locations and narrow date ranges.

pages.title: Rendlesham Files
pages.summary: The Rendlesham incident appears across memoranda and later correspondence, showing how one event was copied, reframed and debated inside government.

pages.title: Weather Records
pages.summary: Meteorological files can help test whether balloons, clouds, meteors or atmospheric effects match the date and place of a reported sighting.

pages.title: Canada Files
pages.summary: Canada's historical UFO records offer a separate national trail of military and civil documentation for comparing official reporting practices.

pages.title: Agency Trail
pages.summary: Canadian UFO reports often passed from witnesses to police, defence and scientific offices, creating uneven but traceable documentary trails.

pages.title: Falcon Lake
pages.summary: Falcon Lake produced medical, police and laboratory records, yet conflicting details prevented officials from reaching a final explanation.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Canada Files.

pages.title: Project Magnet
pages.summary: Project Magnet used government facilities to test Wilbert Smith's ideas about geomagnetism, propulsion and reported flying saucers.

pages.title: Second Storey
pages.summary: Project Second Storey reviewed Canadian UFO reports and concluded that a major continuing investigation was not justified.

pages.title: Shag Harbour
pages.summary: The Shag Harbour files confirm a serious search for a possible aviation emergency without identifying the reported lights.

pages.title: Database Comparison
pages.summary: Database totals and unexplained rates cannot be compared fairly until differences in intake, geography, investigation, classification, and access are

pages.title: Choose a Database
pages.summary: The best source depends on whether the goal is to study witness behaviour, investigated cases, official decisions or source trails.

pages.title: Duplicates
pages.summary: One widely seen light can become many database entries unless reports are carefully grouped into a single event.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Database Comparison.

pages.title: Archive Totals
pages.summary: Archive catalogues count preserved folders, photographs and correspondence, not a consistent number of sky events.

pages.title: Case Counts
pages.summary: A UFO database row may represent a witness report, an investigated event, a source citation or an entire archival file.

pages.title: Unexplained Rates
pages.summary: An unexplained rate reflects each program's intake rules, evidence standards and classification language rather than a universal mystery score.

pages.title: Duplicates
pages.summary: One incident can appear in several databases or through multiple witnesses, creating false clusters unless records are carefully matched and deduplicated.

pages.title: False Patterns
pages.summary: Repeated records can manufacture apparent clusters, surges and statistical significance by giving one well-documented event excessive weight.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Duplicates.

pages.title: Matching Reports
pages.summary: Reliable matching combines time, place, movement, narrative details and source history rather than relying on one identical field.

pages.title: Record Multiplication
pages.summary: One sighting can multiply across witness submissions, investigator files and later publications without becoming several independent events.

pages.title: UFOCAT Counts
pages.summary: UFOCAT preserves multiple references to the same sighting, so its total entries cannot be treated as a count of independent cases.

pages.title: Witness Counting
pages.summary: Independent witnesses may strengthen a case while still representing one event for statistical counting and mapping.

pages.title: GEIPAN
pages.summary: GEIPAN separates identified, poorly documented, and genuinely unresolved cases through a public investigation and classification system.

pages.title: Aircraft Cases
pages.summary: GEIPAN tests whether lighting, perspective and terrain can make an ordinary aircraft appear stationary, saucer-shaped or beam-like.

pages.title: Reclassification
pages.summary: Reinvestigations, better tools and stricter standards can move old Class D files into identified or inconclusive categories.

pages.title: Class C
pages.summary: Class C means investigators lacked reliable evidence, not that they found a strong mystery that resisted explanation.

pages.title: Class D
pages.summary: A sighting reaches Class D only when its residual strangeness is high and the supporting information is judged sufficiently consistent.

pages.title: Case Statistics
pages.summary: GEIPAN's percentages describe classified reports and evidence quality, not the frequency of unexplained objects in French airspace.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on GEIPAN.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on UFO Report Databases.

pages.title: Unidentified
pages.summary: A case remains unidentified when available evidence does not support a satisfactory explanation, which is not the same as confirming an extraordinary craft.

pages.title: Go Fast Parallax
pages.summary: Reconstructing viewing geometry showed that the GoFast object's apparent speed was partly an effect of motion parallax.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Unidentified.

pages.title: Infrared Effects
pages.summary: Glare, tracking changes and shifting heat contrast can make ordinary objects seem to accelerate, vanish or change shape.

pages.title: Starlink Pilots
pages.summary: Five commercial pilots reported unusual Pacific lights later matched to newly launched Starlink satellites under rare viewing conditions.

pages.title: Unresolved Totals
pages.summary: An unresolved percentage mixes strong resistant cases with reports that simply lack enough information for confident identification.

pages.title: Missing Metadata
pages.summary: A striking UFO video may remain unresolved when distance, camera settings, platform motion or original files are missing.

pages.title: MUFON
pages.summary: MUFON cases may include interviews, images, and investigator findings, although paid access and uneven volunteer work limit transparency.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on MUFON.

pages.title: Case File Quality
pages.summary: The most useful MUFON files combine original media, precise timing, independent witnesses and a documented process for eliminating explanations.

pages.title: Historic Records
pages.summary: Digitization can preserve historic reports, but it cannot recreate missing attachments, undocumented decisions or fields never recorded on paper.

pages.title: Investigator Checks
pages.summary: MUFON investigators compare witness accounts with aircraft, astronomy, weather, satellites and image clues before leaving a case unresolved.

pages.title: Member Access
pages.summary: Paid access opens searchable reports and selected attachments, but confidential witness details and internal case records remain restricted.

pages.title: Unexplained Labels
pages.summary: An unexplained MUFON case may reflect unusual evidence, but it can also result from missing data, weak imagery or an unavailable witness.

pages.title: NUFORC
pages.summary: NUFORC offers an unusually large collection of witness accounts, but its patterns reflect reporting behavior as well as events in the sky.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on NUFORC.

pages.title: Review Limits
pages.summary: NUFORC categories and quality tiers add useful context, but they do not turn witness estimates into uniformly investigated conclusions.

pages.title: Date Gaps
pages.summary: A UFO report's event date and posting date can tell very different stories about when sightings and reporting surges occurred.

pages.title: Hotspot Bias
pages.summary: Clusters of NUFORC reports may arise from population, dark skies and viewing opportunity as much as from unusual aerial events.

pages.title: Attention Surges
pages.summary: News coverage, online interest and wider social conditions can increase UFO submissions without any matching rise in aerial phenomena.

pages.title: Self Selection
pages.summary: NUFORC totals reflect who chooses to report, not a random sample of everyone who sees something unusual in the sky.

pages.title: Blue Book
pages.summary: Project Blue Book preserved thousands of military-era reports, but an unidentified ruling meant no satisfactory explanation was reached, not that aliens were

pages.title: The 701 Cases
pages.summary: The 701 cases were a mixed residual set of reports with different witnesses, evidence quality and reasons for remaining inconclusive.

pages.title: Investigation Checks
pages.summary: Investigators compared reports with flights, balloons, astronomy, weather and radar records before deciding whether a case remained unresolved.

pages.title: Unidentified Label
pages.summary: An unidentified ruling meant investigators lacked a confident conventional match, not that the Air Force had confirmed alien technology.

pages.title: Cold War Context
pages.summary: Air defence concerns influenced which sightings drew attention, what investigators checked and how military context entered the surviving files.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Blue Book.

pages.title: Report 14
pages.summary: The statistical study found differences between known and unknown reports but could not determine whether those differences reflected unusual objects or

pages.title: Reports vs Files
pages.summary: A first-hand account records what someone says they saw, while an investigated file adds checks, context, competing explanations, and a documented conclusion.

pages.title: Blue Book Files
pages.summary: Blue Book case files let readers compare original testimony with the Air Force's explanation, paperwork and investigative priorities.

pages.title: Independent Witnesses
pages.summary: Several reports strengthen a UFO case only when witnesses observed separately and did not shape one another's accounts.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Reports vs Files.

pages.title: Distance Errors
pages.summary: Without a reliable distance estimate, dramatic claims about a UFO's physical size or speed cannot be calculated securely.

pages.title: Viewing Geometry
pages.summary: Maps, compass bearings and visible horizons can test whether a reported UFO path matches aircraft, satellites or celestial objects.

pages.title: Unexplained Cases
pages.summary: A case may remain open because evidence is missing, contradictory or genuinely resistant to identification after investigation.

pages.title: Search by Date
pages.summary: A strong date-based search checks public reports, investigated cases, government files, and local context without assuming matching entries are independent.

pages.title: Duplicate Reports
pages.summary: Several catalogue entries may describe one shared event, one copied account, or genuinely separate observations from different locations.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Search by Date.

pages.title: Airfield Records
pages.summary: Searching nearby bases, airfields, police forces, and military districts can uncover records filed under institutions rather than the witness's town.

pages.title: Time Shifts
pages.summary: A sighting near midnight can appear on different dates once local time, daylight saving rules, and UTC are reconciled.

pages.title: Newspaper Check
pages.summary: Local newspapers can reveal police calls, meteors, aircraft activity, outages, and publicity surrounding a reported sighting.

pages.title: Search Radius
pages.summary: Nearby towns, counties, roads, and border regions can reveal related reports that an exact-place search misses.

pages.title: Report Maps
pages.summary: Maps can reveal where reports concentrate, but population, publicity, database reach, and repeated records can create misleading hotspots.

pages.title: Busy Airspace
pages.summary: Busy airspace can increase unfamiliar lights, observer attention, and report volume without proving that anomalous objects prefer those locations.

pages.title: Database Maps
pages.summary: The same world can look very different when one catalogue uses public submissions and another relies on government investigation.

pages.title: Geocoding Bias
pages.summary: Geocoding broad place names to a single downtown point can make scattered reports look like a concentrated urban hotspot.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Report Maps.

pages.title: Small Numbers
pages.summary: A few reports can produce an eye-catching per-capita rate in a small county even when the underlying evidence is thin.

pages.title: Time Filters
pages.summary: A permanent-looking cluster may disappear when reports are grouped by hour, revealing one shared meteor, satellite train, balloon, or re-entry.

pages.title: Reporting Bias
pages.summary: Public UFO databases measure who chooses to report and under what conditions, not the true frequency of unexplained objects.

pages.title: Confidential Channels
pages.summary: Confidential reporting systems can produce sudden increases by releasing testimony that witnesses previously withheld, without any rise in sightings.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Reporting Bias.

pages.title: Online Reporting
pages.summary: Online forms lowered the effort needed to report a sighting, changing who entered the record and making long-term totals harder to compare.

pages.title: Pilot Silence
pages.summary: Pilots may see unusual aerial events more often than most people yet report less because professional stigma can outweigh the value of speaking up.

pages.title: Memory Changes
pages.summary: News coverage, familiar UFO imagery and repeated retelling can become mixed with an older observation before a witness finally submits it.

pages.title: Per Capita Rates
pages.summary: Dividing sightings by population adjusts for observer numbers but cannot correct unequal sky access, tourism, internet use or willingness to report.

pages.title: UFOCAT
pages.summary: UFOCAT connects reports scattered across books, periodicals, investigator files, and older databases, but its entries often require source-by-source

pages.title: Archive Differences
pages.summary: UFOCAT links records across private files, publications and official documents, while government archives preserve custody and administrative context.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on UFOCAT.

pages.title: Database Rescue
pages.summary: UFOCAT survived through copied tapes, damaged backups and format conversions carried out across informal research and institutional networks.

pages.title: Duplicate Entries
pages.summary: UFOCAT may list one event several times because each record can represent a different source in the same documentary chain.

pages.title: Access Levels
pages.summary: UFOCAT distinguishes open files, restricted witness records and confidential cases, shaping what researchers can verify for themselves.

pages.title: Source Trails
pages.summary: Direct and indirect source fields help readers follow a published UFO story toward earlier interviews, witness forms and investigator files.

pages.title: US Archives
pages.summary: The US National Archives brings together UFO and UAP records from many agencies, formats, and record groups beyond Project Blue Book.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on US Archives.

pages.title: JAL 1628 Files
pages.summary: FAA records on Japan Airlines Flight 1628 preserve an aviation-centered view of the 1986 Alaska encounter, including traffic-control and public-information

pages.title: Bulk UAP Data
pages.summary: NARA's bulk packages combine digital files with JSON metadata, but they require substantial cleaning before they can support statistical or computational study.

pages.title: Record Group 615
pages.summary: Record Group 615 creates a central UAP collection without replacing the older agency files where the original records remain.

pages.title: Search Beyond Blue
pages.summary: Useful UFO records are scattered across aviation, intelligence, naval, space, diplomatic and public-affairs collections rather than one master file.

pages.title: Redacted Records
pages.summary: A listed UAP series may include public redactions, sealed attachments or postponed records that are not yet available for full inspection.
